mathematics.assertion_tested: For the explicitly enumerated benchmark targets, uniform annular surface-density elements with declared vertical exponential or sech-squared profiles give signed Newtonian midplane R*dPhi/dR consistent with independent angular/radial quadrature, analytic thin disks/rings, the published exponential-disk Bessel formula, and quadrature refinement within the recorded tolerances.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: IEEE-754 binary64, scipy special functions and deterministic quadrature; no interval certification
mathematics.conventions: R,a,z,height in kpc; nonnegative annular source masses in solar masses; output is signed (km/s)^2 per solar mass, not velocity. G=4.30091e-6 kpc (km/s)^2 per solar mass unless explicitly overridden. Positive output is inward radial attraction; exterior annuli may have negative output. Each source bin has constant surface density M/[pi*(b^2-a^2)] and exactly normalized vertical profile over the declared numerical vertical support. No spherical replacement or local stellar-template rescaling.
inputs: Analytic test disks/rings and explicitly listed benchmark radii in benchmark_kernel.py
vertical laws exp(-abs(z)/h)/(2h) and sech(z/h)^2/(2h), with h given as geometry; h=0 is the razor-thin limit
Uniform annulus boundary integral, derived directly from Newtonian Green function by the planar divergence theorem
non_claims: No unique density or physical detection is implied by positive source feasibility
No fitted thickness, smoothing parameter, force coupling or stellar gradient
No certified global floating-point error bound
Numerical vertical-tail truncation is explicitly controlled and is not a fitted physical cutoff
No claim for arbitrary unresolved radial structure outside the declared annular basis
Published formula agreement is a numerical implementation check, not an observational geometry authentication
